item.title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
item.guid: title:reading writing sharing and interacting with the world through video
item.description: A Video Is a Trace of a World TL; DR. We treat a video as a partial, lossy, time-ordered observation of a world that keeps evolving whether or not the camera sees it. Four operations connect the two — reading (video → world), writing (world → video), sharing (one model does both), and interacting (the world advances under actions) — and they organize video understanding, video generation, unified models, and video world models in one account. The hard part is not rendering convincing frames; it is showing evidence that a model tracks the world behind them. Paper: https://arxiv. org/abs/2610.

item.title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence
item.guid: title:kimi k3 open frontier intelligence
item.description: Today, we are introducing Kimi K3 — our most capable model. Kimi K3 is a 2. 8T-parameter model built on our Kimi Delta Attention and Attention Residuals, with native vision capabilities and a 1-million-token context window. It is the world's first open 3T-class model, designed for frontier intelligence across long-horizon coding, knowledge work, and reasoning. While its overall performance still trails the most powerful proprietary models, Claude Fable 5 and GPT 5. 6 Sol, Kimi K3 demonstrated frontier-level performance across our evaluation suite, consistently outperforming other tested models.

item.title: From self-serve AI to real architecture — what a PM learns by building the pipeline himself
item.guid: title:from self serve ai to real architecture what a pm learns by building the pipeline himself
item.description: Two voices run through this piece: the PM intrigued by what AI changes for a DevSecOps agile team, and the tinkerer who built the whole thing himself just to understand it. Neither one is trying to convince you of anything — just to tell the story. This isn't meant to be academic or professional. It's the story of a personal exploration: how a plain, everyday need — stop wasting hours comparing prices by hand — dragged me from a single chat prompt all the way to a small multi-agent app running on a server. At every step, two voices talk to each other in my head. I'm keeping them separate here, on purpose.

item.title: Building Crash-Safe Agent Workflows with Pi Durable and SQLite
item.guid: title:building crash safe agent workflows with pi durable and sqlite
item.description: Moving autonomous coding agents out of interactive terminal loops and into unattended background workers exposes a brutal operational reality. When your Node process receives an unhandled SIGKILL, suffers an out-of-memory crash, or restarts during a multi-file refactoring sequence, standard stateless agent runtimes leave behind corrupted workspace directories, half-applied git patches, and lost conversation ledger trees. Developers quickly realize that an off-the-shelf loop is wholly unsuited for production deployment on container platforms or dedicated cloud VMs. Building crash-safe agent workflows with pi durable and sqlite bridges this gap by introducing atomic transaction boundaries and durable state persistence directly into the TypeScript runtime. We faced this exact failure mode last month when an automated migration agent crashed midway through a 400-file Abstract Syntax Tree transformation. Because the session state lived entirely in volatile memory, the process restart wiped out the execution ledger, leaving the repository in an ambiguous state where half the modules were migrated while the rest held stale references.

item.title: Introducing PerceptionBench
item.guid: title:introducing perceptionbench
item.description: Evaluating Atomic Visual Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models Authors Kimi Team We are releasing PerceptionBench , a benchmark that isolates visual perception and evaluates it as a set of atomic capabilities— discovered from how today's models fail, not defined in advance. From frontier-model failures across 42 benchmarks, we derive 10 atomic perceptual capabilities and construct 3,000 verified questions, each isolating a single capability and answerable by looking, with no reasoning or external knowledge required.

item.title: The Interpretability team studies how large language models work internally as a foundation for AI safety. They seek to understand what happens inside neural networks so that we can better trust the models we build.
item.guid: title:the interpretability team studies how large language models work internally as a foundation for ai safety they seek to understand what happens inside neural networks so that we can better trust the models we build
item.description: It’s hard to reason about the safety of neural networks without understanding what happens inside them. Our goal is to be able to explain large language models’ behavior, and to use that understanding to identify problems that are hard to see from the outside, such as situations where a model’s stated reasoning differs from what it’s actually doing. Our early work focused on mapping the internal mechanisms of AI models. Today, we increasingly apply our methods to real models to understand how they think and why they behave the way they do. We’ve developed techniques that allow us to understand models’ inner workings in plain language, making it easier to detect unsafe behavior or dishonest reasoning and safeguard against it. item.title: Why Technology Decisions Fail Without Strong Business Alignment
item.guid: title:why technology decisions fail without strong business alignment
item.description: Most failed technology decisions are not failures of technology. They are failures of alignment. The project shipped, the vendor delivered, the architecture was sound, and the business still got nothing it could measure. In 2026, with AI absorbing the budget faster than any technology in a generation, the gap between what gets built and what the business actually needs has become the most expensive problem in the enterprise, and the one leaders are still least willing to name. The Comfortable Lie About Why Projects Fail When a technology initiative collapses, the post-mortem almost always points at the technology. The platform was wrong.

item.title: A New Transformer for TEMPORAL Attention #ai
item.guid: title:a new transformer for temporal attention ai
item.description: A new temporal causal reasoning former (TCR-Former) with a modified temporal attention mechanism. Note: One of the new elements is a separate "event slot", or multiples of them (128). An event slot is a learned numerical representation of a potential event from the text itself, not the event itself, not a timestamp alone, and not a causal rule. Its sole purpose is to gather event information into a form that can be temporally supervised and supplied to the decoder. Another way to see it is that each event slot is kind of an additional feature vector for temporal causal reasoning. Its intended purpose is to collect information about one potential event from the document and provide that information to the reasoning decoder.

item.title: I Trained Qwen 4B with Distillation to Catch Qwen 27B
item.guid: title:i trained qwen 4b with distillation to catch qwen 27b
item.description: Can a 27 billion parameter model teach a 4 billion model to be as good as itself? Last time, RL got Qwen 4B from 52% to 58. 4% and then hit a wall. This time I used Qwen 27B as a teacher and tried all three kinds of distillation on two DGX Sparks: training on the teacher's answers, training on its probabilities, and on-policy distillation where the 27B grades every token the 4B writes. item.title: Kimi Introduces Agent Swarm: Let 100 AI Agents Work for You
item.guid: title:kimi introduces agent swarm let 100 ai agents work for you
item.description: In 2025, if you walked into any AI conference, you may hear the same gospel: faster inference, longer context windows, cheaper inference costs. It's as if we've spent years perfecting the hammer, making it lighter, stronger, more precisely balanced, while never questioning the fact that the carpenter still has only two hands and twenty-four hours in a day. Now, Kimi introduces Agent Swarm. It is not a better hammer. It is a reconstruction of the entire workshop.
